request: Implement the researched Jev Ultrafast integration in BB Surf. Natural-language browser tasks must be able to execute through the upstream Jev indexed-action loop against the project's existing Steel browser, while Playwright remains available for deterministic navigation, explicit inspect/click/fill/press actions, and safe preflight-only fallback. Preserve project isolation, human-control handoff, explicit per-run paid-call authorization, no replay after uncertain mutation, and independent outcome verification. First identify what is missing or incomplete in the existing adapter, capture a Playwright-versus-Jev behavioral and latency baseline on representative supported local tasks without paid calls unless separately authorized, make the smallest complete code change, add behavior-level tests, update accurate docs, run focused and root verification, install/reload the local plugin, and verify the real BB Surf CLI/browser surface. Do not remove Playwright or change the default engine without evidence that Jev wins on both completion and latency.
message: Implemented and committed native Jev and text-model API key settings, per-key saved-setting precedence over optional private dotenv values, safe frontend behavior, docs, and behavioral tests. The steel-browser check passed (SDK types, typecheck, 62 tests, build), reload and real settings UI inspection passed, and an explicitly authorized live Jev run completed on example.com in 2839ms total / 295ms agent loop with independent page inspection confirming the expected page. Commit 8e9f26ac was pushed to the feature branch. Target sync was attempted and refused solely because unrelated pre-existing Empirical archive changes keep the shared worktree dirty; those changes were preserved and excluded.
